reasons: Only three of six sections are visible, so most of the file cannot be checked.

terms.meaning: A named group of projects chosen for the same reason, here A for new gas plants, B for coal-to-gas conversions, and subject for the projects being benchmarked.
Combined-cycle gas turbine, a gas plant that uses a gas turbine and a steam turbine together.
A coal plant that has been rebuilt to run on natural gas.
The utility whose projects are being compared. The code uses the abbreviation without spelling it out.
A fixed list of records that the import uses to match each research result to the right project.

sections.name: File setup, GasPowerCohort
sections.title: Purpose and project cohorts
sections.what: The header explains that this file lists the US gas-power projects being benchmarked. It also defines three cohort labels. Nothing is shown to users directly.
sections.why: The header says the cohorts were set by user direction on 2026-10-23.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new cohort means updating this type as well, or the code will reject it.

sections.name: GasPowerIdentity
sections.title: Shape of one gas-power identity
sections.what: Defines the fields a gas-power identity has: its state, cohort, whether it is a new build, conversion or repowering, and which APS project it is compared against. These fields add to the shared population identity.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared identity does not cover gas-specific details, so these are added here.
sections.watch_out: The project type is set by the helper below, not stored separately, so the helper and this type must agree.

sections.name: id
sections.title: Building one identity with defaults
sections.what: Creates one identity from its key, name, state, site and cohort. It sets the segment and project type from the cohort or from one specific key, and sets the APS project it is compared against.
sections.why: The conversion rule is tied to cohort B and one specific key, which suggests those two are the only conversions in the list.
sections.watch_out: A conversion placed in another cohort without that key would be labelled as a new build.

sections.name: GAS_POWER_US_IDENTITIES
sections.title: US gas power project list
sections.what: The fixed list of US gas-fired power projects that researchers are asked to study, one entry per project, each with a name, state, site and batch code. Two entries are marked as subject projects that the benchmark is built around, and a few entries carry a note listing existing database rows that were checked and found to be different projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list keeps every research run aimed at the same projects, so repeat runs do not pick up new ones by accident. The meaning of the A and B labels is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Keys must stay unique across the list, and an existing key should not be renamed once its project exists, because the project ID is built from it.

sections.name: GAS_POWER_COMPANY_NAMES
sections.title: Company spelling lookup for gas
sections.what: A small lookup that maps four alternative spellings of two utility companies to one standard name each, so the database keeps one company row per company.
sections.why: The code comment says it avoids duplicate company rows.
sections.watch_out: Any new spelling a researcher uses must be added here, or it will create a second company row.

sections.name: GAS_POWER_POPULATION
sections.title: Settings for gas power import
sections.what: The settings that tell the shared importer how to treat the gas power list: the industry name, batch naming, the words ignored when checking for duplicate names, how location and cohort are written, and the company lookup. It is exported under a standard name so the importer finds it automatically.
sections.why: The code comment says changing any field changes the committed plan digests, so these settings should not be edited casually.
sections.watch_out: Changing the ID namespace after rows exist changes every project ID for this list.

summary: Defines the list of US gas-power projects to research, each with a fixed key, name, state, site and cohort, so that researcher replies land on the same records.
purpose: Identity list for the US gas-power population import, used as a benchmark comparison set.
why: The header says keys are given to the researchers so their replies match these identities, and that new rows get fixed IDs so later batches update the same rows.
how: Defines the three cohort labels and the identity shape. A shared helper builds each identity and sets its segment and project type from the cohort or the key. The rest of the file, which is not shown in full here, lists the projects and their population settings.
inputs: None at run time. The list is typed in by hand.
outputs: A list of gas-power identity records for the population import. The population settings file that these records feed is not visible here.
risks: Only the first three sections are visible, so the project list and population settings are not checked here. A conversion project placed in the wrong cohort without its key will be labelled as a new build.
debug: If a conversion project shows as a new build, check its cohort and key in the helper. If a project has the wrong state or site, check its entry in the list.
